headline: A 2023 law that renews federal anti-trafficking programs, sets up a national strategy on cybercrime against individuals, and expands human trafficking data sharing and collection.
what_it_does: The law reauthorizes several federal programs that fight human trafficking, which extends their legal authority. It requires a national strategy to address cybercrime committed against individuals. It also expands rules for sharing information and collecting data about human trafficking.

who_it_affects.group: People who have been or may be victims of human trafficking
who_it_affects.how: Federal anti-trafficking programs that the law reauthorizes are meant to keep serving them.

who_it_affects.group: Federal agencies that run anti-trafficking programs
who_it_affects.how: They must continue these programs under the reauthorized authority and follow the new information-sharing and data-collection requirements.

who_it_affects.group: Law enforcement agencies working on trafficking cases
who_it_affects.how: They may share and collect trafficking information under the expanded rules.
The required national strategy is meant to address cybercrime against individuals.

when_it_takes_effect: Enacted January 5, 2023. The official summary does not list separate effective dates for each provision.
